newjerseyMock.q: What is a useful practice target for the New Jersey knowledge test?
choices: 40 of 50 correct, or 80%
10 of 50 correct
Any score because there is no pass mark
newjerseyMock.explanation: The NJ Driver Manual describes a 50-question knowledge test and an 80% passing standard.

newjerseyMock.q: For New Jersey practice, this sign means:
choices: A lane will end or narrow ahead
The road becomes one-way
A rest area begins ahead
newjerseyMock.explanation: Lane Ends signs warn you to prepare for a lane reduction and merge safely. This page uses original artwork; verify final rules in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: What hazard does this sign warn about?
choices: Low tire pressure checkpoint
Slippery road surface when wet
A required speed increase
newjerseyMock.explanation: Slippery road signs warn that traction may be reduced, especially when wet. This page uses original artwork; verify final rules in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: This sign marks or warns of:
choices: A railroad crossing
A bus-only lane
A school parking lot
newjerseyMock.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn drivers to look, listen, and never stop on tracks. This page uses original artwork; verify final rules in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: For New Jersey practice, what does this orange sign usually mean?
choices: Road work or temporary traffic control
A scenic route ahead
A hospital zone
newjerseyMock.explanation: Orange signs usually mark construction, maintenance, or temporary traffic patterns. This page uses original artwork; verify final rules in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: This sign warns that ahead there is:
choices: A traffic signal
A toll booth only
A dead-end street
newjerseyMock.explanation: Signal Ahead signs warn drivers to prepare for a traffic light. This page uses original artwork; verify final rules in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: What does this sign warn about?
choices: A divided roadway or median begins
A bridge is closed
Only emergency vehicles may enter
newjerseyMock.explanation: Divided highway signs warn that a median or divider changes the roadway layout. This page uses original artwork; verify final rules in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: For New Jersey practice, this sign means drivers should not:
choices: Pass other vehicles in this zone
Use headlights
Drive under the speed limit
newjerseyMock.explanation: Do Not Pass signs mark places where passing is not allowed or is unsafe. This page uses original artwork; verify final rules in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In a work zone, drivers should:
choices: Slow down, follow signs, and watch for workers and equipment
Maintain normal speed if no worker is visible
Ignore temporary lane markings
newjerseyMock.explanation: Work zones often have temporary traffic patterns, narrow lanes, and workers close to traffic. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: If you are being passed, you should:
choices: Maintain speed or slow slightly and keep right
Speed up to block the pass
Move left without signaling
newjerseyMock.explanation: Help the pass happen safely by holding steady and staying right when appropriate. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: Driving after alcohol, cannabis, or impairing medicine is dangerous because it:
choices: Slows reaction time and judgment
Improves night vision
Makes lane changes easier
newjerseyMock.explanation: Impairing substances reduce judgment, coordination, attention, and reaction time. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: Before opening a vehicle door next to traffic, you should:
choices: Check mirrors and look for vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians
Open quickly so traffic notices
Only check the front windshield
newjerseyMock.explanation: Dooring can injure bicyclists and other road users. Check before opening the door. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: If a vehicle behind you wants to pass on a two-lane road, you should:
choices: Keep right and do not increase speed
Move toward the center line
Brake suddenly
newjerseyMock.explanation: Stay predictable and give the passing driver room when a pass is legal and safe. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: A blind spot is:
choices: An area around your vehicle not visible in mirrors
Only the space directly under the car
A lane where headlights are not required
newjerseyMock.explanation: Mirrors do not show every area, so drivers need a quick shoulder check before moving. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, when roads are icy, the best first adjustment is to:
choices: Slow down and avoid sudden steering or braking
Use cruise control
Follow closer so you can see tire tracks
newjerseyMock.explanation: Smooth, slow inputs help reduce skids on ice. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: If a tire blows out, you should:
choices: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow gradually
Brake hard immediately
Turn sharply off the road
newjerseyMock.explanation: Keep control first, then slow down gradually and move off the roadway when safe. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: A bicyclist in the roadway should be treated as:
choices: A road user who may need space and caution
A pedestrian who must always leave the lane
An obstacle you should pass without changing speed
newjerseyMock.explanation: Drivers must share the road and pass bicyclists carefully under state law. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, when backing out of a driveway, you should:
choices: Look in all directions and back slowly
Use only the backup camera
Back quickly so traffic stops
newjerseyMock.explanation: Backup cameras help, but they do not replace looking around and moving slowly. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: If your vehicle starts to skid, the safest general response is to:
choices: Ease off pedals and steer where you want the vehicle to go
Brake as hard as possible
Close your eyes until it stops
newjerseyMock.explanation: Avoid sudden inputs and steer toward the path you want as traction returns. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, at a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian waiting or crossing, you should:
choices: Slow and yield as required by law
Wave the pedestrian across without checking other lanes
Continue if you are already at the speed limit
newjerseyMock.explanation: Slow early, yield when required, and make sure other lanes are safe too. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, at a stop sign, what should you do?
choices: Stop completely before the limit line or crosswalk
Slow down only if traffic is coming
Tap the horn and continue
newjerseyMock.explanation: A stop sign requires a complete stop before moving only when it is safe. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, at a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, who should usually go first?
choices: The driver on the right
The larger vehicle
The driver who waves first
newjerseyMock.explanation: When vehicles arrive together, the driver on the right usually has the right of way unless another rule or sign applies. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: A solid yellow line on your side of the road usually means:
choices: Passing is not allowed from your lane
You may pass whenever the road is clear
The lane is reserved for buses
newjerseyMock.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side normally means do not pass from that lane. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, the safest general response is to:
choices: Pull to the right and stop when safe
Speed up to stay ahead of it
Stop immediately in your lane without checking traffic
newjerseyMock.explanation: Move right and stop when it is safe so the emergency vehicle can pass. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: Before changing lanes, you should:
choices: Signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder
Signal only after moving
Rely only on the rearview mirror
newjerseyMock.explanation: Safe lane changes require a signal, mirror check, and blind-spot check. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, when driving in fog, which choice is usually safest?
choices: Use low-beam headlights and slow down
Use high beams so you can see farther
Drive close to the vehicle ahead
newjerseyMock.explanation: Low beams reduce glare in fog, and slower speed gives more time to react. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: A pedestrian is crossing at an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection. You should:
choices: Yield and let the pedestrian cross safely
Honk so the pedestrian stops
Drive through if you are below the speed limit
newjerseyMock.explanation: Drivers must watch for and yield to pedestrians where the law gives them the right of way. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: What does a red curb usually mean?
choices: Loading zone for passengers only
Parking allowed for a short time
No stopping, standing, or parking
newjerseyMock.explanation: Red curb markings usually identify a no stopping, standing, or parking area. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what should you do first?
choices: Ease off the accelerator and steer straight
Brake hard immediately
Turn sharply toward the shoulder
newjerseyMock.explanation: Ease off the accelerator and keep steering steady until traction returns. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, at night, you should dim high beams for approaching traffic because:
choices: Bright lights can blind other drivers
High beams use too much battery power
It makes your car easier to hear
newjerseyMock.explanation: High beams can reduce another driver's ability to see the road safely. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: If a school bus ahead has flashing red lights, the safest general response is to:
choices: Stop as required and watch for children
Pass quickly before children step out
Move into the left lane and keep driving
newjerseyMock.explanation: Flashing red school-bus lights mean children may be entering or leaving the bus. Stop when required by law. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: Which choice best describes defensive driving?
choices: Expecting hazards and leaving yourself time to react
Driving faster than traffic to avoid clusters
Using the horn whenever traffic slows
newjerseyMock.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning ahead, expecting mistakes, and keeping space around your vehicle. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, when parking uphill with a curb, your front wheels should generally be turned:
choices: Toward the curb
Straight ahead only
Away from the curb
newjerseyMock.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so the curb can help stop the vehicle if it rolls. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?
choices: Increase following distance from the car ahead and let the tailgater pass when safe
Tap your brakes repeatedly
Speed up until the tailgater disappears
newjerseyMock.explanation: Create more space ahead and avoid sudden braking. Let the other driver pass when it is safe. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: Before entering a roundabout, you should:
choices: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout
Stop inside the roundabout to check signs
Enter quickly because entering traffic has priority
newjerseyMock.explanation: Drivers entering a roundabout generally yield to traffic already circulating. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: If traffic signals are not working, you should usually treat the intersection as:
choices: A four-way stop unless an officer directs otherwise
A green light for the busiest street
A no-stop intersection
newjerseyMock.explanation: When signals fail, stop and proceed carefully unless a law officer or temporary control directs traffic. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: A safe following distance should increase when:
choices: Roads are wet, visibility is poor, or traffic is heavy
You are in a hurry
The vehicle ahead is new
newjerseyMock.explanation: Poor conditions require more time and distance to stop safely. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

newjerseyMock.q: In New Jersey, when a traffic light turns yellow as you approach, you should:
choices: Stop if you can do so safely
Always speed up
Change lanes immediately
newjerseyMock.explanation: A steady yellow light warns that red is next. Stop safely if there is time and distance. Confirm exact wording in the New Jersey Driver Manual.

roadSignsCore.q: What should a driver do at this sign?
choices: Slow down only if traffic is present
Come to a complete stop and yield before moving
Yield only to pedestrians
Continue if the intersection looks clear
roadSignsCore.explanation: A stop sign requires a complete stop. After stopping, yield to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

roadSignsCore.q: This triangular sign means drivers should:
choices: Let other traffic go first when needed
Stop every time for at least three seconds
Turn around immediately
Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
roadSignsCore.explanation: A yield sign tells you to slow down and give the right of way when another road user has priority.

roadSignsCore.q: What does this red and white sign tell a driver?
choices: The lane is for carpools only
The road is closed only at night
Do not drive into this roadway or ramp
One-way traffic begins after the next block
roadSignsCore.explanation: Do Not Enter is a regulatory warning against entering a roadway, ramp, or lane from the wrong direction.

roadSignsCore.q: If you see this sign after turning, what is the safest action?
choices: Keep driving until the next intersection
Pull over safely and correct your direction when safe
Increase speed to leave the area quickly
Turn on high beams and continue
roadSignsCore.explanation: A Wrong Way sign means you are facing traffic. Slow down, move out of the travel lane if possible, and correct course safely.

roadSignsCore.q: What movement is prohibited by this sign?
choices: A left turn
A right turn on red
A lane change
A U-turn
roadSignsCore.explanation: The red slash over the U-turn symbol means that U-turns are not allowed at that location.

roadSignsCore.q: This black and white arrow sign means:
choices: Traffic moves only in the arrow direction
A detour begins ahead
Passing is allowed on both sides
The shoulder is open for driving
roadSignsCore.explanation: A One Way sign tells drivers the required direction of traffic on that street or lane.

roadSignsCore.q: What does this sign set for the road segment?
choices: A suggested speed for curves only
A minimum speed in bad weather
A legal maximum speed limit
A truck-only speed limit
roadSignsCore.explanation: Speed limit signs are regulatory signs. They state the legal maximum speed under normal conditions.

roadSignsCore.q: What does this pennant-style sign mean?
choices: No passing is allowed in this zone
Emergency vehicles only
Road narrows ahead
No parking on the shoulder
roadSignsCore.explanation: Do Not Pass signs mark areas where passing another vehicle is prohibited because visibility or road layout is unsafe.

roadSignsCore.q: What should this yellow sign make you expect?
choices: A mandatory stop
Traffic entering or joining your lane
A hospital entrance
A no-passing zone
roadSignsCore.explanation: Merge signs warn that traffic streams may join. Check mirrors, manage speed, and leave space.

roadSignsCore.q: This sign warns that:
choices: A lane will end and traffic must merge
A new lane begins for passing
Only buses may use the lane
A toll lane starts ahead
roadSignsCore.explanation: Lane Ends signs warn that a travel lane will disappear, so drivers should merge early and smoothly.

roadSignsCore.q: What driving adjustment fits this sign?
choices: Brake hard to test traction
Use cruise control in rain
Slow down and avoid sudden steering or braking
Drive on the shoulder
roadSignsCore.explanation: Slippery When Wet warns of reduced traction. Lower speed and make gradual inputs, especially in rain.

roadSignsCore.q: This sign means drivers should prepare for:
choices: A traffic signal ahead
A railroad crossing only
A speed limit change
A one-way street
roadSignsCore.explanation: A signal ahead sign warns that a traffic light is coming up, often where visibility or stopping distance matters.

roadSignsCore.q: What does this divided-highway sign indicate?
choices: The road becomes gravel
A median or divider begins ahead
The lane is for bicycles only
All traffic must turn left
roadSignsCore.explanation: This sign warns that the roadway will be divided by a median or barrier ahead.

roadSignsCore.q: What should you expect after this circular warning sign?
choices: A pedestrian bridge
A truck route
A railroad crossing ahead
A tunnel entrance
roadSignsCore.explanation: The round railroad advance warning sign tells drivers to prepare for tracks and follow any crossing signals or gates.

roadSignsCore.q: This yellow-green sign warns about:
choices: Children or school pedestrians crossing
A college parking lot
A bus-only lane
A playground entrance with no road crossing
roadSignsCore.explanation: School crossing signs warn drivers to slow down, scan carefully, and obey school-zone rules where posted.

roadSignsCore.q: What does this pedestrian sign call for?
choices: Speed up before the crosswalk
Watch for people crossing and be ready to yield
Honk before entering the crosswalk
Use the opposing lane to pass stopped cars
roadSignsCore.explanation: Pedestrian crossing signs warn that people may be in or near the crosswalk. Be ready to slow or yield.

roadSignsCore.q: This orange sign usually means:
choices: Road work or maintenance activity ahead
A permanent speed limit increase
A scenic overlook
A hospital zone
roadSignsCore.explanation: Orange signs are commonly used for temporary traffic control, construction, maintenance, or work-zone activity.

roadSignsCore.q: This service sign points drivers toward:
choices: A no-parking area
A nearby hospital or medical service
A school crossing
A divided highway
roadSignsCore.explanation: Blue service signs help drivers find services such as hospitals, fuel, food, lodging, or rest areas.

roadSignsCore.q: What is the main message of this roundabout sign?
choices: A tunnel begins
Two-way traffic ends
A circular intersection is ahead
Only emergency vehicles may enter
roadSignsCore.explanation: A roundabout sign warns that traffic will circulate around a central island. Slow down and yield as required.

roadSignsCore.q: This animal crossing sign means drivers should:
choices: Expect possible animal movement near the road
Stop only if a police officer is present
Drive faster to pass the area quickly
Use the lane only for hunting access
roadSignsCore.explanation: Animal crossing signs warn that animals may enter the roadway. Reduce speed and scan shoulders carefully.

roadSignsCore.q: Which color and shape pattern is most associated with regulatory signs?
choices: Blue circle with service symbols
White rectangle with black or red rules
Orange diamond with recreation symbols
Brown rectangle with school-zone symbols
roadSignsCore.explanation: Many regulatory signs use white rectangles with black text or red restrictions. Stop, yield, and do-not-enter signs are special regulatory cases.

roadSignsCore.q: Which sign category usually warns about road conditions rather than stating a law?
choices: Warning signs
Regulatory signs
Parking signs only
Route marker signs only
roadSignsCore.explanation: Warning signs usually alert drivers to conditions ahead, such as merging traffic, curves, pedestrians, signals, or slippery roads.

roadSignsCore.q: When a sign uses a red circle and slash over a symbol, it usually means:
choices: The action is recommended
The action is prohibited
The road is scenic
The route number changed
roadSignsCore.explanation: A red circle and diagonal slash is a common prohibition symbol, telling drivers that the pictured action is not allowed.

roadSignsCore.q: Why should permit-test practice include both sign meaning and driver action?
roadSignsCore.imageAlt: Yield sign used in a driver action question
choices: Because signs only matter on highways
Because test questions often ask what to do, not just what the sign is called
Because colors are never tested
Because state manuals do not explain signs
roadSignsCore.explanation: A useful practice round connects each sign to the safe action: stop, yield, merge, slow, watch, or avoid a prohibited movement.

roadSignsChallenge.q: What should a driver do before entering this curve?
choices: Reduce speed before the road bends
Stop in the travel lane
Move onto the shoulder
Accelerate through the curve
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: A curve warning sign gives advance notice of a change in road alignment. Slow before the curve and keep a steady lane position.

roadSignsChallenge.q: This winding-road sign warns drivers to expect:
choices: One sharp turn followed by a stop sign
Several curves over the next road section
A road closed to passenger vehicles
A passing lane on every curve
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: Winding Road warns of a series of curves. Lower speed, look through each bend, and avoid passing where sight distance is limited.

roadSignsChallenge.q: What does this crossroad symbol tell you?
choices: The road becomes one way
A railroad crosses the highway
Another road crosses ahead
The highway ends immediately
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: A Crossroad sign shows that another road intersects ahead. Scan both sides and be ready for entering or crossing traffic.

roadSignsChallenge.q: Where should you expect traffic to enter after this sign?
roadSignsChallenge.imageAlt: Yellow side road intersection warning sign
choices: From the side shown by the branch
Only from a driveway behind you
From a railroad track
From the median only
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: A Side Road sign shows the direction from which another road joins. Watch that side for vehicles entering the main road.

roadSignsChallenge.q: What driving decision is coming at this T-intersection sign?
choices: Continue straight at the same speed
Prepare to turn left or right because the road ends
Merge into a lane on the right
Stop for a railroad crossing
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: A T-Intersection sign warns that your road ends at another road. Slow down and prepare for the required turn and right-of-way check.

choices: Two lanes move in your direction
Passing is required on the left
Opposing traffic begins or continues ahead
The road becomes a divided highway
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: Two-Way Traffic warns that vehicles will travel in opposite directions. Stay right and expect oncoming traffic.

roadSignsChallenge.q: What should you begin doing when you see this warning sign?
choices: Prepare to stop completely at the stop sign ahead
Stop immediately beside the warning sign
Treat the next intersection as a yield
Speed up before traffic reaches the stop sign
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: Stop Ahead gives advance notice when a stop sign may not be visible soon enough. Begin slowing so you can make a complete stop at the actual stop sign.

roadSignsChallenge.q: What hazard does this bicycle sign warn about?
choices: A bicycle-only parking area
Bicyclists may enter or cross the roadway
Motorcycles must leave the highway
Bicycles have a separate speed limit
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: A Bicycle warning sign alerts drivers to possible bicycle entry or crossing activity. Slow down, scan carefully, and allow safe space.

roadSignsChallenge.q: At a roundabout warning sign, which action should come first?
choices: Choose an exit after entering at full speed
Stop in the circulating lane
Slow down and look for traffic already circulating
Turn left around the central island
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: A roundabout warning sign means a circular intersection is ahead. Reduce speed, follow lane markings, and yield as required before entering.

roadSignsChallenge.q: Why is a school crossing sign a speed-control clue?
choices: Children can be less predictable and local school-zone rules may apply
School signs always cancel the posted speed limit
Only school buses may use the road
Drivers must stop whenever the sign is visible
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: School crossing signs call for extra scanning and controlled speed. Obey any posted school-zone limit and be ready for children crossing.

roadSignsChallenge.q: What is the safest response if railroad warning lights begin flashing?
choices: Cross quickly before the gate lowers
Stop as required and never drive around a lowered gate
Stop with the front wheels on the tracks
Follow the vehicle ahead even if space is blocked
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: Flashing railroad signals require drivers to stop as directed. Never go around a lowered gate or enter tracks without room to clear them.

roadSignsChallenge.q: Which clue separates a temporary work-zone warning from a permanent warning sign?
choices: Its orange background
Its blue service symbol
Its red octagon shape
Its brown recreation color
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: Orange is used for temporary traffic-control and work-zone warnings. Expect changed lanes, workers, equipment, or temporary directions.

roadSignsChallenge.q: On a wet road, why should you avoid sudden braking after this sign?
choices: Hard braking increases tire traction
Reduced traction can cause skidding or loss of control
The sign means the road is closed
The sign applies only to trucks
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: Slippery When Wet warns that tire grip may be reduced. Lower speed and make steering, braking, and acceleration changes gradually.

roadSignsChallenge.q: When traffic is merging, what creates the safest gap?
choices: Matching traffic speed while adjusting space early
Stopping in the through lane
Blocking the merging lane
Driving beside another vehicle through the merge point
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: A merge warning calls for early speed and space management. Avoid staying beside another vehicle where the lanes join.

roadSignsChallenge.q: Can you always drive at the posted speed shown here?
choices: Yes, even when visibility is poor
Yes, if other vehicles are faster
No, unsafe conditions can require a lower speed
No, the sign is only a suggested minimum
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: A speed limit is the legal maximum under normal conditions. Rain, darkness, traffic, curves, or limited visibility can require a slower safe speed.

roadSignsChallenge.q: What should you do when a no-passing zone begins before a hill or curve?
choices: Finish any pass only if you can do so without entering the prohibited zone
Start a pass because traffic is slower uphill
Use the shoulder to pass
Ignore the sign when the center line is visible
roadSignsChallenge.explanation: A no-passing zone marks limited sight distance or another unsafe condition. Do not begin a pass that would continue into the prohibited area.

regulatorySignsCore.q: Which driver action does this sign require?
choices: Slow only if another vehicle is close
Come to a complete stop, then yield before moving
Continue after tapping the brakes
Stop only when a pedestrian is visible
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: A stop sign is a regulatory sign. It requires a complete stop and a right-of-way check before proceeding.

regulatorySignsCore.q: At this sign, what should you be ready to do?
choices: Give the right of way when another road user has priority
Stop for three seconds every time
Turn around because the road is closed
Accelerate to enter first
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: Yield means slow down and let other traffic or pedestrians go first when they have the right of way.

choices: Only trucks may enter
The next road is one way in your direction
Do not enter this roadway or ramp
Parking is prohibited after the sign
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: Do Not Enter is a regulatory sign that prohibits entry into that road, ramp, or direction of travel.

regulatorySignsCore.q: If you see this sign while driving, the safest meaning is:
choices: You are traveling against allowed traffic direction
A detour begins in two miles
Passing is not allowed
A work zone begins ahead
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: Wrong Way warns that you are facing traffic. Slow, avoid continuing in the lane, and correct direction safely.

regulatorySignsCore.q: What movement is not allowed at this sign?
choices: Changing lanes
A U-turn
Going straight
Stopping before a crosswalk
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: The red slash over the U-turn symbol means U-turns are prohibited at that location.

regulatorySignsCore.q: This sign controls traffic by telling drivers:
choices: Traffic may move only in the arrow direction
A lane ends ahead
No turns are allowed for one block
The road is for emergency vehicles only
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: One Way signs are regulatory signs that establish the required direction of traffic.

choices: A suggested speed for heavy rain only
A legal maximum speed under normal conditions
A minimum passing speed
A work-zone detour route
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: Speed limit signs state the legal maximum speed for normal conditions. Drivers may need to go slower when conditions are unsafe.

choices: Passing another vehicle in this zone
Stopping at the shoulder
Entering a highway
Turning right after stopping
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: Do Not Pass marks a zone where passing is not allowed because road layout, traffic, or sight distance makes it unsafe.

regulatorySignsCore.q: What does the 4-WAY plaque change about this stop sign?
choices: Every approach has a stop sign, so drivers must stop and use right-of-way order
Only the first car at the intersection must stop
Drivers may roll through if no one honks
It is a warning sign, not a rule sign
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: A 4-Way Stop still requires a complete stop. The plaque tells you the other approaches also stop, so arrival order and right-of-way matter.

regulatorySignsCore.q: At this sign, what movement is prohibited?
choices: Turning right from this approach
Going straight through the intersection
Stopping before the crosswalk
Driving in the right lane
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: No Right Turn is a regulatory sign. The key action is that a right turn is not allowed where the sign is posted.

regulatorySignsCore.q: At this sign, what should a driver do while the signal is red?
choices: Wait for a signal that allows the turn
Turn right after stopping if no traffic is visible
Turn only if another driver waves you through
Treat it as a yield sign
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: No Turn on Red means stopping first is not enough. The turn is prohibited while the signal is red.

regulatorySignsCore.q: This sign tells a driver to:
choices: Stay to the right of an island, divider, or obstruction
Use the right lane only for passing
Turn right at the next intersection
Prepare for a soft shoulder
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: Keep Right is a regulatory direction sign. It tells traffic which side of an island, divider, or obstruction to use.

regulatorySignsCore.q: Which sign color pattern most often means a rule or restriction?
choices: Brown and white
Blue and white
Red, white, or black on white
Orange and black only
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: Regulatory signs often use red, white, black, or black text on a white background. They tell drivers about rules and restrictions.

regulatorySignsCore.q: A regulatory sign is different from a warning sign because it usually:
choices: States a law, limit, restriction, or required movement
Only describes scenic routes
Warns about a possible hazard without stating a rule
Shows nearby gas, food, or hospitals
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what is required, prohibited, or limited. Warning signs alert drivers to conditions ahead.

regulatorySignsCore.q: When you see a red circle and diagonal slash over a symbol, it usually means:
choices: The action is optional
The action is prohibited
The action is recommended during rain
The road is scenic
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: A red circle with a slash is a common prohibition symbol. The action shown by the symbol is not allowed.

regulatorySignsCore.q: What is the most useful way to study regulatory traffic signs for a permit test?
regulatorySignsCore.imageAlt: Yield sign used for permit-test strategy
choices: Memorize color only and ignore driver action
Connect each sign to the action it requires or prohibits
Study only blue service signs
Skip state handbook wording completely
regulatorySignsCore.explanation: Permit-test questions often ask what a driver should do. Pair each regulatory sign with the required or prohibited action.

trustPages.title: About TestDayTools
trustPages.description: Learn what TestDayTools is, how the site is maintained, and why all tools are unofficial.

content.heading: What we make
content.text: TestDayTools is a small, independent website that turns test logistics into quick tools: dates, checklists, score guides, and practice pages.

content.heading: How we work
content.text: Pages are built from simple data files so dates, FAQs, checklists, and practice questions can be updated without redesigning the site.

content.heading: Editorial approach
content.text: The site favors practical planning details: what to check, what to bring, what to verify, and which official source should make the final call.

content.heading: How DMV pages are built
content.text: DMV facts are checked against official agency pages where possible. Public learner discussions and search demand are used only to identify confusing language and real planning gaps, not as authority for rules.

content.heading: What makes the tools original
content.text: Practice questions, checklists, mistake-log categories, road-sign illustrations, and study paths are written for TestDayTools. They are designed to turn a missed answer or document problem into a next step.

content.heading: What we do not publish
content.text: The site does not publish official test questions, copied forum posts, scraped competitor quizzes, hidden redirects, or claims that a practice score guarantees a permit or license outcome.

content.heading: Corrections and updates
content.text: Dates and policies can change. When a page depends on official timing, the source link is included so readers can verify the latest rule before acting.

content.heading: Funding and editorial independence
content.text: TestDayTools is currently self-funded. If advertising is added, ads will be separated from quiz controls and will not determine practice answers, source selection, rankings, or editorial conclusions.

content.heading: Affiliation
content.text: We are not affiliated with College Board, AP, SAT, any DMV, or any government agency. Names are used only to describe the exams and public services students are researching.

trustPages.title: Editorial Policy
trustPages.description: How TestDayTools writes, checks, updates, and labels unofficial DMV, AP, and SAT tools.

content.heading: Purpose
content.text: TestDayTools publishes practical planning tools, checklists, and original practice questions for exam and DMV preparation. The goal is to help readers decide the next action, not to replace official sources.

content.heading: Original tools and questions
content.text: Practice questions, sign illustrations, checklists, and study flows are written for this site. DMV sign graphics are simplified original SVG illustrations used for recognition practice.

content.heading: User-confusion research
content.text: Forum threads, search suggestions, and trend signals can reveal what learners are actually confused about, such as course-vs-exam steps, online test results, documents, appointments, road signs, or retest rules. Those signals influence page structure, but facts still come from official sources.

content.heading: No copied answer keys
content.text: The site does not copy official permit-test questions, private answer keys, Reddit comments, or competitor quiz items. Practice content is written as study material and labeled as unofficial.

content.heading: Tool-first writing standard
content.text: A page should help the reader decide what to do next: open an official source, drill one weak sign group, log a mistake, check documents, or stop practicing and handle appointment logistics.

content.heading: Official-source priority
content.text: When a page mentions a rule, test format, document requirement, or deadline, the official source is treated as the final authority. If a TestDayTools page conflicts with an official source, the official source wins.

content.heading: Update process
content.text: Static pages are rebuilt from structured data files so dates, source links, FAQs, and practice paths can be updated without redesigning the site. Pages show a site-wide last-updated date.

content.heading: Corrections
content.text: Correction requests should include the page URL, the section that appears outdated or unclear, and the official source that should be checked.

content.heading: Advertising policy
content.text: Advertising is not installed yet. If ads are approved, placements will stay separate from quiz choices, checklist controls, source links, and required tool buttons. Advertising will not change practice answers, source selection, rankings, or editorial conclusions.

trustPages.title: Privacy Policy
trustPages.description: Privacy policy for TestDayTools, including browser storage, Google Analytics, hosting logs, and future advertising disclosures.

content.heading: Personal information
content.text: TestDayTools does not provide user accounts or forms that ask you to submit names, emails, test scores, driver's license numbers, Social Security numbers, payment details, or school records. Hosting and analytics services may still process limited technical data as described below.

content.heading: Quiz answers
content.text: Practice quiz answers are checked in your browser. They are not submitted to a server by this static site.

content.heading: Checklist and mistake-log storage
content.text: Some tools can remember selected states, checked items, or saved weak areas in your browser's local storage. This is meant only for convenience on the same device and is not an official DMV record.

content.heading: No driver's license data
content.text: Do not enter driver's license numbers, Social Security numbers, birth dates, addresses, payment details, or appointment confirmation numbers into this site. Use official agency pages for personal applications.

content.heading: External official-source links
content.text: Many pages link to official DMV, College Board, or other agency resources. Those sites have their own privacy practices and may ask for account or application information.

content.heading: Server logs
content.text: Because the site is hosted as static pages, the hosting provider may process basic technical logs such as page requests, device information, or IP-derived region for security and delivery.

content.heading: Google Analytics
content.text: The site uses Google Analytics 4 to measure basic site usage, including page views, traffic sources, device and browser information, approximate region, scrolling, downloads, tool actions, and outbound clicks. Google Analytics may use cookies or similar identifiers and process technical information under Google's own terms and privacy practices. TestDayTools uses these measurements to decide which study tools need improvement and does not send names, emails, driver's license numbers, account details, or test scores to Google Analytics.

content.heading: Advertising
content.text: Advertising is not installed yet. If Google AdSense is activated, third-party vendors including Google may use cookies to serve ads based on a visitor's prior visits to TestDayTools or other websites. Google's use of advertising cookies enables Google and its partners to serve, limit, personalize, and measure ads. Any additional advertising vendors used by TestDayTools will be disclosed before their code goes live.

content.heading: Advertising choices and consent
content.text: Visitors can manage or opt out of personalized Google advertising through Google Ads Settings. Before eligible advertising is activated for visitors in the EEA, the United Kingdom, or Switzerland, TestDayTools will configure a Google-certified consent management platform and provide the disclosures and choices required for that traffic.

content.heading: Children and students
content.text: The site is a general-audience educational resource and does not ask students to create accounts, submit scores, or provide school records. Learners should not enter personal application, identity, payment, or school information into any TestDayTools study control.

links.label: Google: How Google uses information from sites that use its services

trustPages.title: Accessibility
trustPages.description: Accessibility practices and feedback options for TestDayTools quizzes, checklists, tables, and printable study resources.

content.heading: Our approach
content.text: TestDayTools aims to make study tools usable with a keyboard, screen reader, browser zoom, and common mobile and desktop layouts. Core quizzes and checklists do not require an account or drag-and-drop interaction.

content.heading: Keyboard and controls
content.text: Interactive choices use native buttons, links, inputs, checkboxes, and select controls where practical. Focus indicators remain visible, and a skip link lets keyboard users move directly to the main content.

content.heading: Road-sign illustrations
content.text: Road-sign practice uses original simplified illustrations with text alternatives. Meaning is explained in text after each answer, so color alone is not the only way to identify the rule or driver action.

content.heading: Responsive tables and zoom
content.text: Pages are designed to reflow on mobile screens and at browser zoom. Wide date or requirements tables use a horizontal scroll area so columns remain readable instead of overlapping.

content.heading: Printable resources
content.text: Printable resources keep headings, sign names, and meanings in text. Print layout is a convenience layer; the same information remains available in the standard web page.

content.heading: Known limitations and feedback
content.text: Accessibility can vary by browser, assistive technology, and device. If a control, table, illustration, or download is difficult to use, send the page URL, the affected element, and your browser or assistive technology through the contact page so the issue can be reproduced and corrected.

trustPages.title: Contact
trustPages.description: Contact information and correction requests for TestDayTools.

content.heading: Corrections
content.text: If you find an outdated date, broken source link, unclear explanation, accessibility problem, or DMV-source mismatch, open a correction report through the public GitHub issue link below. This creates a visible record that can be checked and closed after the page is corrected.

content.heading: Best correction reports
content.text: The most useful reports include the page URL, the exact heading or question that seems wrong, the official source link, and a short note about why the page should change.

content.heading: DMV and exam account issues
content.text: TestDayTools cannot access DMV, DPS, MVC, FLHSMV, College Board, SAT, AP, testing-provider, appointment, payment, or score accounts. Use official support channels for personal records.

content.heading: Correction reports are public
content.text: GitHub issue reports are public. Do not include names, email addresses, account details, test scores, driver's license information, school records, appointment details, or other personal information.

content.heading: No official support
content.text: For official AP, SAT, score, registration, permit, or license questions, contact College Board or the relevant DMV directly.

content.heading: Advertising and privacy
content.text: Advertising is not installed yet. If ads are approved, placements will stay away from quiz answer buttons and required tool controls, and the Privacy Policy and consent settings will be reviewed before launch.

trustPages.title: Disclaimer
trustPages.description: Important unofficial-site disclaimer for TestDayTools AP, SAT, and DMV study pages.

content.heading: Unofficial site
content.text: TestDayTools is fan-made and unofficial. It is not affiliated with College Board, AP, SAT, any DMV, or any government agency.

content.heading: No guarantees
content.text: Dates, policies, and rules can change. Use official sources for final decisions about exam registration, score sending, credit, permits, and licensing.

content.heading: DMV rules vary by state and applicant path
content.text: Permit, learner license, REAL ID, document, appointment, testing-provider, retest, age, and parent-consent rules can vary by state, county office, applicant age, and license path.

content.heading: Official sources decide final requirements
content.text: A TestDayTools checklist can help organize the task, but the state agency, official manual, testing provider, service center, or school office decides what is accepted for your situation.

content.heading: Practice questions
content.text: DMV practice questions on this site are original study questions. They are not copied from official permit tests and cannot guarantee a passing score.

content.heading: Not legal or academic advice
content.text: The site provides general planning information only. A school, college, testing organization, or DMV should make the final decision for your situation.

content.heading: Source priority
content.text: If TestDayTools conflicts with an official source, treat the official source as correct and send a correction request so the page can be reviewed.
